llm.summary: This is a coherent document-to-poster tool, but its installer and HTML rendering pipeline create security risks that users should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: Large ML/OCR dependencies, Chromium, outbound LLM/image API calls, and configurable API endpoints are mostly purpose-aligned, but the combination handles user documents and credentials with limited containment guidance.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is disclosed, but install.sh and SKILL.md use an unverified remote curl-to-shell UV installer, install system packages with apt-get, install Playwright Chromium, and requirements.txt includes an unpinned Git dependency.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill asks the model to generate full HTML from user documents and then writes that HTML directly; conversion can load the result in a JavaScript-enabled Chromium context, so document-influenced model output may execute active browser content during PDF/PNG generation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifacts create a virtual environment, install user/system dependencies, install Chromium, and create a .env template; I did not find background services, scheduled tasks, backdoors, or unrelated persistence.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is PDF/Markdown parsing, LLM-based HTML poster generation, multi-format conversion, and Gemini-style image generation; the inspected code largely matches that purpose, including local parsing, external LLM calls, and output file generation.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use a sandbox or disposable environment, avoid running install.sh as root, replace curl-to-shell installation with verified packages, remove or pin the Git dependency, update vulnerable dependency pins, and only process documents you trust unless JavaScript is disabled and generated HTML is sanitized before conversion.
llm.findings:
[T03] unexpected: Installing UV is purpose-related, but piping a mutable remote installer directly into sh is an avoidable high-impact supply-chain risk.
[T08] unexpected: The mutable git+https dependency in requirements.txt is not necessary given the pinned marker-pdf dependency in pyproject.toml and uv.lock.txt.
[T09] unexpected: Rendering HTML is core functionality, but executing untrusted LLM-generated HTML in a JavaScript-enabled browser without sanitization or request blocking is under-contained.
[SC4] unexpected: ML/OCR dependencies are expected, but the scanner-reported vulnerable pinned versions are a material supply-chain concern rather than evidence of malicious intent.
[TT3] expected: Environment-configured LLM endpoints and API-key headers are expected for OpenAI-compatible backends, though users must only configure trusted endpoints because document contents are sent there.
[PE3] expected: The .env references are API-key configuration templates and environment loading, not standalone evidence of credential theft.
[TP4] expected: I did not validate the scanner's claim that SKILL.md materially misstates the implementation; the inspected documentation and code both describe PDF/Markdown parsing, LLM rendering, conversion outputs, and Gemini-style image generation.
